ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points $A$, $B$, $C$ are on the circle $\odot O$, $\angle ACB=105^\circ$, then what is the value of $\angle \alpha$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let's take any point $D$ on the major arc $AB$ and connect $AD$ and $BD$,\\
since quadrilateral $ACBD$ is inscribed in circle $O$, and $\angle ACB=105^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ADB=180^\circ-\angle C=180^\circ-105^\circ=75^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle AOB=2\angle ADB=2\times 75^\circ=150^\circ$.\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{150^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a circle with O as the center; the three points A, C, and B are all on the circle; A is on the left side, C is above and slightly to the left, and B is on the right side. The chords CA and CB are drawn in the figure, as well as the two radii OA and OB from the center O connected respectively to A and B. α is marked at point O, and is the smaller central angle between OA and OB. Reasoning: It is known that ∠ACB = 105°. ∠ACB is an inscribed angle, and what it subtends is the arc AB that does not contain C, that is, the larger arc AB. By the inscribed angle theorem, the measure of this arc is 2 × 105° = 210°. The whole circle is 360°, so the measure of the other smaller arc AB is 360° − 210° = 150°. α is the smaller central angle corresponding to this smaller arc AB, therefore α = 150°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a circle centered at O, with A, C, B lying on the upper part of the circle and radii OA and OB drawn. The marked angle α is the smaller central angle ∠AOB, whose intercepted arc is the minor arc AB passing through C. From the text, ∠ACB = 105°. By the inscribed angle theorem, ∠ACB intercepts the arc AB that does not contain C, i.e. the major arc AB, so that major arc has measure 2×105° = 210°. The minor arc AB, and hence the smaller central angle α, is 360° − 210° = 150°.
